claims.text: The initial material is a disordered, multielement crystalline magnetic high-entropy alloy with moderate coercivity.
A high-pressure nitrogen anneal can incorporate approximately 1 at.% interstitial nitrogen into the alloy.
Interstitial nitrogen insertion induces local lattice distortions.
Interstitial nitrogen creates controlled lattice strain.
The nitrogen-induced lattice strain enhances domain-wall pinning.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning increases the coercive field.
Introducing approximately 1 at.% interstitial nitrogen will increase coercive field relative to an undoped matched baseline.
The coercivity increase is expected during room-temperature magnetic hysteresis cycling under standard measurement conditions.
The effect is expected to apply to similarly structured magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Changes in alloy composition or processing may alter the coercivity outcome.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement may depend on processing parameters and alloy composition.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as receiving no nitrogen anneal, whereas the experimental control is described as being processed identically except for nitrogen exposure. These imply different controls: no anneal versus a matched anneal under a non-nitrogen atmosphere.
